memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When someone has a burn on their skin and a reddish-white or white spot appears in the raw flesh of the burn, the priest is to examine the spot, and if the hair in it has turned white, and it appears to be more than skin deep, it is a defiling disease that has broken out in the burn. The priest shall pronounce them unclean; it is a defiling skin disease." - Lev 13:24-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now the same careful examination is applied to a burn. Not a disease this time, but an injury — something that happened to the person, not something that arose within them.

That distinction matters pastorally. Some of what we carry we brought on ourselves. But some of it was done to us. The harsh father. The betrayal by a friend. The words spoken over us as children that we still hear. The loss that came without warning. These are burns. We did not choose them.

And God's instruction is exactly the same: bring it to the priest. Let it be examined. Because a burn, left unattended, can develop into something else. Grief can curdle into bitterness. A wound we never processed can shape how we treat everyone who comes after.

Hebrews warns us to see to it that no bitter root grows up to cause trouble and defile many (Heb 12:15). Note the word defile — the same territory this chapter has been walking. And note the word many. Untended pain rarely stays with one person.

God is not asking you to pretend the burn never happened. He is asking you to bring it to Him rather than let something worse grow in it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What burn in your life came from someone else's actions?
2. Has anything begun to grow in that wounded place that concerns you?
3. What would it mean to bring that pain honestly to God this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You know the wounds I did not choose. Guard my heart from bitterness taking root in them, and bring Your healing to the places that still ache. Amen.
